titles.TOM-48: Polygon draw tool (an adapter over leaflet-editable)
titles.TOM-94: Capability guide and presentation with evidence from the running app

summaries.TOM-5: The foundation epic: the pnpm monorepo, the shared Zod contracts, both databases, CI and the docs skeleton that every other lane started from.
summaries.TOM-6: The database epic: the Drizzle schema for areas, versions and the audit log on PostGIS, with the spatial index, geodesic area, seeding and retention.
summaries.TOM-7: The auth and security epic: Better Auth on Workers, one session check for REST and the WebSocket upgrade, validation, rate limiting, timeouts and health checks.
summaries.TOM-8: The areas API epic: create, read in bounds, update with optimistic concurrency, soft delete, version history, caching, audit and the OpenAPI document.
summaries.TOM-9: The realtime epic: one Room Durable Object per map on the hibernation API, carrying presence, live drafts, the fan-out of saved changes and reconnect recovery.
summaries.TOM-10: The frontend epic: the React and Leaflet app with its design system, the auth screens, the draw tool, the aerial layer and the live collaboration UI.
summaries.TOM-11: The quality epic: unit, integration and two-browser end-to-end tests, the load test, the README and the decision records.
summaries.TOM-12: The deployment epic: one Cloudflare Worker serving the API, the Durable Objects and the SPA, reaching Neon through Hyperdrive and hardened for production.
summaries.TOM-13: Set up the pnpm workspace with the web app, the API Worker and the shared package, so every later task had a place to land.
summaries.TOM-14: Published the shared Zod schemas and types for areas, API errors and the WebSocket envelope, used on both sides of every boundary.
summaries.TOM-15: Brought up a local PostGIS in Docker Compose and a Neon project with PostGIS, and wired Hyperdrive's local connection for development.
summaries.TOM-16: Added the GitHub Actions workflow that lints, type-checks, tests and dry-runs the Worker deploy on every pull request.
summaries.TOM-17: Started the README outline, the decision record template and the process log that the later tasks kept current.
summaries.TOM-18: Defined the areas, area versions and audit log tables with a WGS84 polygon column, plus the auth tables, as Drizzle schema and migrations.
summaries.TOM-19: Set the migration path: migrations run from CI over the direct database URL, while the Worker reaches the database through Hyperdrive.
summaries.TOM-20: Added the partial GiST index and the bounds query that returns only the live areas intersecting the viewport.
summaries.TOM-21: Computed each area in square kilometres on the spheroid through PostGIS geography, so the stored value is geodesic rather than planar.
summaries.TOM-22: Wrote an idempotent, batched seed of more than 10,000 valid polygons inside Israel's bounds for tests and benchmarks.
summaries.TOM-23: Made deletes soft and added a daily Cron Trigger that purges areas deleted more than seven days ago.
summaries.TOM-24: Measured the bounds query on 10,000 rows with and without the spatial index and recorded the numbers in the benchmarks document.
summaries.TOM-25: Ran Better Auth with email and password on Hono in the Worker through the Drizzle adapter, after a short spike showed it fits the platform.
summaries.TOM-26: Added the session middleware and reused the same check to gate the WebSocket upgrade before a socket reaches the Room.
summaries.TOM-27: Allowed only the app's own origin to send credentials and added secure response headers.
summaries.TOM-28: Validated every request at the boundary with the shared schemas and enforced the polygon rules: a closed ring, vertex limits, coordinate ranges and no self-intersection.
summaries.TOM-29: Built an exact per-user sliding-window limiter in a Durable Object, 50 drawing actions a minute, answered with 429 and a retry time.
summaries.TOM-30: Bounded every request with a timeout that also aborts its database work and answers 504 when it fires.
summaries.TOM-31: Returned one error shape from a central handler, hid internals on server errors and logged structured JSON lines with a request id.
summaries.TOM-32: Added a liveness endpoint and a readiness endpoint that checks the database and the Room.
summaries.TOM-33: Created the Room Durable Object that accepts the map's WebSockets on the hibernation API, so an idle room costs nothing.
summaries.TOM-34: Handled the protocol messages inside the Room with schema validation, a size cap and an error frame for anything unknown.
summaries.TOM-35: Derived the presence list from the sockets' own attachments, so it survives the Room hibernating.
summaries.TOM-36: Relayed drawings in progress to the other users as throttled, sequence-numbered updates and dropped stale frames.
summaries.TOM-37: Sent every saved create, update and delete from the API to the Room, the single coordinator per map, with no external pub/sub.
summaries.TOM-38: Kept connections honest with pings answered without waking the Room and a sweep that drops sockets gone quiet.
summaries.TOM-39: Handled lost connections with backoff, a resync after reconnecting and polling while offline, with a banner that names the state.
summaries.TOM-40: Charged drawing on the socket to the same per-user budget as the REST writes and refused the excess with an error frame.
summaries.TOM-41: Wrote the decision record on scaling out on Cloudflare: one Durable Object per room, sharding, and what hibernation costs.
summaries.TOM-42: Scaffolded the React app on Vite with TanStack Router and Query, carrying the session in the router so the map route is protected.
summaries.TOM-43: Built the register, sign-in and sign-out screens on Better Auth's React client.
summaries.TOM-44: Mounted a Leaflet 1.9.4 map with OpenStreetMap tiles, separate panes for areas and drafts, and a debounced viewport.
summaries.TOM-45: Investigated how to show govmap's aerial tiles, served on the Israeli TM grid, beside OpenStreetMap, and confirmed the CRS-swap approach.
summaries.TOM-46: Added the aerial layer on its own projection, with tested conversions between the Israeli grid and WGS84.
summaries.TOM-47: Switched base layers with a crossfade while keeping the view, the saved areas and any drawing in progress across the change of projection.
summaries.TOM-48: Built the polygon draw tool, which after three rulings became a thin adapter over a maintained editing plugin, with the realtime protocol kept in-house.
summaries.TOM-49: Showed the area live while drawing and compared it with the server's value after saving.
summaries.TOM-50: Loaded the areas in view, drew them, saved optimistically and offered a two-button choice when a save meets a newer version.
summaries.TOM-51: Connected the map to the Room: who is online, other users' drawings as ghost shapes, and saved changes patched into the cache.
summaries.TOM-52: Added the side panel that lists the areas in view, with inline rename, version history and revert.
summaries.TOM-53: Polished the layout, the loading and error states, focus handling, contrast and reduced motion after a usability and accessibility audit.
summaries.TOM-54: Created areas in one transaction that validates the polygon, stores its area, writes version 1 and the audit row, then tells the Room.
summaries.TOM-55: Served the areas inside a bounding box with a row limit, leaving geometry simplification out by decision.
summaries.TOM-56: Updated an area only when the client's version matches, answering a stale write with 409 and the current server copy.
summaries.TOM-57: Deleted areas softly with an audit row, so they leave the map at once and stay recoverable until the purge.
summaries.TOM-58: Listed an area's versions and reverted to an old one by writing it as a new version, never rewriting history.
summaries.TOM-59: Cached viewport reads in the Workers Cache API under keys stamped with the map's version, so a write makes the old entries unreachable.
summaries.TOM-60: Wrote an audit row for every mutation and for drawing sessions on the socket, without delaying the response.
summaries.TOM-61: Described every route in OpenAPI 3.1 and served a reference UI for the API.
summaries.TOM-62: Covered the core rules with unit tests: area maths, polygon validation, the rate limiter, the conflict path and the projections.
summaries.TOM-63: Ran integration tests for the Worker and the Durable Objects on workerd against a real PostGIS.
summaries.TOM-64: Scripted a two-browser Playwright scenario in which one user draws and the other sees it live.
summaries.TOM-65: Ran the API under wrangler dev in a container beside PostGIS in Docker Compose, so the local stack matches the Workers runtime.
summaries.TOM-66: Wrote the README sections and the architecture decision records.
summaries.TOM-67: Load-tested the REST API and the WebSocket path with k6 and recorded the results.
summaries.TOM-68: Added telemetry: structured logs and Analytics Engine datapoints for database time, sockets and Room traffic.
summaries.TOM-69: Deployed one Worker that serves the API, both Durable Objects and the built SPA as static assets from a single origin.
summaries.TOM-70: Connected production to Neon through Hyperdrive, set the Worker's secrets and separated the environments.
summaries.TOM-71: Planned a preview environment per pull request, then canceled it because a demo app does not need one.
summaries.TOM-72: Checked the Durable Objects in production: the migration tags, hibernation wake-ups in the logs and the checks in the deploy guide.
summaries.TOM-73: Hardened production with trusted origins, secure cookies, a sign-in rate limit, health checks and a documented rollback.
summaries.TOM-74: Applied the M0 milestone code review's findings and the first pull request's review comments in one follow-up pull request.
summaries.TOM-75: Prepared the code for parallel lanes: every M1 dependency installed once, the Durable Object binding, a stub per lane and one constants module.
summaries.TOM-76: Recorded the M1 plan, the design-system brief and decisions D15 to D18 before the lanes started.
summaries.TOM-77: Built the Grid 4 design system: tokens, the UI components and Storybook.
summaries.TOM-78: Joined the M1 lanes on one branch, added the API contract suite to CI, wrote the process log and checked two browsers end to end.
summaries.TOM-79: The post-deployment epic: work set aside on 2026-10-12 so the first production deploy came first, then taken up once it was live.
summaries.TOM-80: Ran every Storybook story as a browser test in CI through the Vitest addon and Playwright.
summaries.TOM-81: Renamed the colour tokens across the open pull requests after the design system replaced the old palette.
summaries.TOM-82: Moved every database read onto the Drizzle query builder, keeping raw SQL for PostGIS fragments and write statements only, with a lint rule to hold the line.
summaries.TOM-83: Turned on Better Auth's cookie cache for five minutes, so most requests skip the session lookup in the database.
summaries.TOM-84: Applied a build-versus-buy audit's cut list inside the open pull requests that owned the files.
summaries.TOM-85: Changed the drawing budget to one action per drawing session instead of one per frame, keeping a per-socket frame rate as the burst guard.
summaries.TOM-86: Applied the verified rows of a whole-codebase simplification review on a stacked branch, removing far more code than it added.
summaries.TOM-87: Made the readiness check fail a deploy that lacks its origin settings, so a deploy run by hand cannot look healthy.
summaries.TOM-88: Stopped the sign-in screen from flashing on a cold load while the session check is still running.
summaries.TOM-90: Moved the pinned Node version to the current LTS line across the Docker image, CI and the engines field.
summaries.TOM-91: Moved the Node pin on to version 26 without waiting for its LTS date.
summaries.TOM-92: Stabilised three tests that timed out or flaked under heavy parallel load.
summaries.TOM-93: Made a reload of a signed-in browser paint the app frame and the map surface first, instead of a blank page or the sign-in screen.
summaries.TOM-94: Produced the capability guide and presentation, with screenshots and measured numbers from the running app.
summaries.TOM-95: Showed author names instead of id prefixes in the history panel and made initials ignore punctuation.
summaries.TOM-96: Rendered unknown paths inside the app frame with a link back, instead of bare text.
summaries.TOM-97: Rewrote the README for a human reader and moved the deep detail into separate documents.
summaries.TOM-98: Styled the header's guide link as a button and kept the header from shifting when the session arrives.
